newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - Sept 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - Sept 13.

text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Friday's Pakistani newspapers.
- Gunmen killed the leader of Pakistani Shi'ite militant group Sipah-i-Mohammad, Murid Abbas Yazdani, at his house in Islamabad on Thursday night.
- Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will visit Islamabad on Friday to hold talks with Pakistani Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto, a foreign ministry spokesman said.

- Afghanistan's rebel Taleban Islamic militia launched a three-pronged attack to take more eastern territory and entered the pro-government Laghman province after Wednesday's capture of the region's main town of Jalalabad.
- Pakistan said it reserved the right to adequately respond to any nuclear escalation by India.
- Prime Minister Bhutto has directed the Punjab provincial government to levy agriculture income tax at flat rates.
- The IMF has told Pakistan to impose agricultural income tax, cut military expenditures, remove regulatory import duties, slash tariffs further and manage flexible exchange rates.
- Former finance minister and secretary general of the opposition Pakistan Muslim Legaue party, Sartaj Aziz, has termed the latest 3.65 percent devaluation of the rupee as "highly alarming".
- Prime Minsiter Bhutto has ruled out the possibility of imposing financial emergency after the devaluation of the rupee.

- A partial strike was observed in some parts of Balochistan province on the call of opposition political parties and government employees, who are demanding restoration of 40 percent state allowance for them.
- Pakistani rice export prices are likely to fall slightly on a proposed sale of 30,000 tonnes of Basmati rice by the state-run Rice Export Corporation of Pakistan on Sunday.
- Pakistan proposes to double the existing trade volume with Indonesia in the next four years, said Shahid Hasan, Special Assistant to the prime minister on ecnomic affairs.
- Pakistan's foreign trade gap narrowed to $500 million, or about 21 percent, in the first two months of fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) from $632 million in July-August of period of 1995/96.
- Prime Minister Bhutto announced a development package of 115 billion rupees for five big cities of Punjab province.
- The Central Board of Revenue has restored the facility of tax-free import of raw materials to be used in the manufacture of exportable goods.
